raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Adds **context-parallel decode scoring** for the AITER fp8 indexer on ROCm (gfx950, fp8 index cache, TP>1, opt-in via `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1`).

Same distributed algorithm as #57832 (Triton bf16 path), adapted for the AITER kernel interface:
- Each rank scores its 1/world_size shard of KV blocks via `pa_sparse_block_score_decode` with a shard block table
- Scores scattered into global-shape `[heads, tokens, max_block]` tensor pre-filled with `-inf`
- MAX allreduce reconstructs all positions from their owning rank
- `pa_sparse_block_topk` runs on the complete allreduced scores

**Default: OFF** (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=False`). Same env var as #57832. AITER path selected when fp8 index cache + gfx950 + TP>1. The per-step allreduce adds latency that only pays off at moderate-to-high concurrency and mid-range context (10k–90k ISL).

### MiniMax-M3 sparse attention pipeline

| Stage | Backend | Index cache dtype | When selected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indexer | Triton (#57832) | `bf16` | `indexer_kv_dtype=bf16` — default |
| Indexer | **AITER** (this PR) | `fp8_e4m3` | `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8` — requires AITER sparse PA |
| Attention | **AITER_SPARSE_PA** | — | `SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1` + `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` |

This PR targets the **AITER fp8 indexer** path. The fp8 MFMA scoring kernel is faster per block than the Triton bf16 path, so CP provides the same absolute latency reduction but against a faster baseline.

## Changes

| File | Type |
|---|---|
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter_cp.py` | New — `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl` |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter.py` | Modified — CP dispatch in `select_aiter_indexer_impl_cls` |
| `vllm/envs.py` | Modified — `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP` (shared with #57832) |

## Test Plan

### Hardware
8× AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), 256 GB HBM3 per GPU, ROCm 6.4 / rocm100

### Image
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19` (vLLM v0.3.1.dev311)

### Server (MXFP4 model weights, AITER fp8 indexer)
```
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB=256
export VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1           # set to 0 for baseline

vllm serve /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --served-model-name amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --port 8766 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --block-size 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --language-model-only \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --max-model-len 130000
```

### Benchmark command
```
vllm bench serve \
  --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --tokenizer /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --base-url http://localhost:8766 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 20000 --random-output-len 512 \
  --max-concurrency 8 --num-prompts 24
```

## Test Result

### MXFP4 Throughput ISL Sweep (vLLM 0.3.1)

**Indexer:** AITER fp8 (`indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`) | **Attention:** AITER_SPARSE_PA (`kv_cache_dtype=fp8`)

| ISL | Baseline (tok/s) | CP Indexer (tok/s) | Delta | TTFT (ms) | p99 TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **20k** | 364.2 | **473.3** | **+29.9%** | 6,130 → 3,281 | 18,095 → **6,612** |
| 64k | 327.5 | 327.1 | −0.1% | 5,052 → 5,025 | 8,196 → 8,161 |
| 100k | 261.9 | 262.7 | +0.3% | 8,494 → 8,430 | 18,794 → 18,623 |

At 20k: **+30% throughput**, **−46% mean TTFT**, **−63% p99 TTFT**.
At 64k+: neutral — AITER sparse attention dominates; indexer is not the bottleneck.

### Comparison: AITER fp8 vs Triton bf16 indexer (both with CP)

| ISL | Triton bf16 CP (#57832) | AITER fp8 CP (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 20k | 466.0 tok/s | **473.3 tok/s** (+2%) |
| 64k | 303.7 tok/s | **327.1 tok/s** (+8%) |
| 100k | 237.4 tok/s | **262.7 tok/s** (+11%) |

The AITER fp8 path is consistently faster due to the fp8 MFMA scoring kernel; the CP delta is similar for both paths.

### Benchmark C — AgentX Pareto Sweep (MXFP4+EAGLE3, TP=4, vLLM 0.3.1)

**Indexer:** AITER fp8 (`indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`) | **Attention:** AITER_SPARSE_PA
**Server:** `max-num-seqs=64`, `enable-chunked-prefill`, `enable-prefix-caching`, EAGLE3 MTP spec decode (`synthetic_acceptance_length=2.78`)
**Benchmark:** aiperf `inferencex-agentx-mvp`, Weka trace `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k`, 900s per point
**Methodology:** Single server per run (baseline then CP back-to-back), 60s warmup — eliminates ISL trace variance.

| Concurrency | Baseline (tok/s/GPU) | CP (tok/s/GPU) | Delta | vs ATOM (MI355X) | ISL baseline | ISL CP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 14,732 | 14,767 | +0.2% | 0.66x | 79,387 | 79,464 |
| 20 | 19,505 | 19,579 | +0.4% | 0.57x | 81,224 | 81,343 |
| 24 | 19,686 | 19,713 | +0.1% | 0.48x | 80,464 | 80,486 |
| 32 | 27,708 | 27,992 | +1.0% | 0.61x | 75,857 | 75,812 |

CP is neutral (0–1%) at all concurrency points with EAGLE3 spec decode. With speculative decoding, decode is fast enough that the indexer is not the bottleneck. The AITER fp8 indexer already scores blocks in ~1/8 the time of a single-rank Triton bf16 scorer; CP further reduces this to ~1/64 — but at these concurrencies and ISLs the attention kernel dominates.

**Hardware note:** Our MI350X vs ATOM/MI355X gap is hardware, not config. CP adds zero overhead in both cases.

**Reference (MI355X TP=4, from [PR #57909](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57909)):**
| Concurrency | ATOM | vLLM+CP (#57909) | Uplift |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 22,276 | 22,022 | 0.99x |
| 20 | 34,277 | 33,682 | 0.98x |
| 24 | 41,155 | 40,556 | 0.99x |
| 32 | 46,211 | 45,973 | 0.99x |

### Correctness

Mathematical equivalence: MAX of non-overlapping partial scores = MAX of full scores. Same algorithm as #57832 (validated with GSM8K 5-shot: 93.5% on both CP=0 and CP=1 with the Triton path).

## Related
- #57832 — Triton bf16 CP indexer (same algorithm, bf16 index cache path)
- #57909 — Upstream CP indexer (Fangzhou/Ai): at conc=20, 98% of ATOM throughput (33,681 vs 34,277 tok/s/GPU)

## PR Pundit Review — [#57840](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57840)

**5 rule violations · 5 architecture concerns · 2 files reviewed**
Rules checked: 32 (27 passed, 5 failed)

---

### 🔴 Blockers

**`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter_cp.py:1-12` — Missing benchmark / description**
This performance-affecting change (new context-parallel AITER indexer for ROCm) provides no reproducible benchmark steps or before/after metrics. Reviewers have consistently blocked such PRs.
> **Fix:** Add before/after latency and `gsm8k` accuracy numbers for the CP AITER indexer path, and reproduce the benchmark command in the PR description.

**`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter.py:601-614` — `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP` not registered in `vllm/envs.py`**
`envs.VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP` is accessed but not declared as a canonical `VLLM_`-prefixed attribute.
> **Fix:** Add `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP: bool = False` to `vllm/envs.py`.

**`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter_cp.py:1-30` — New cross-cutting parallelism mechanism without RFC**
Introduces a new CP indexer dispatch abstraction (`select_aiter_cp_indexer_impl_cls`) as a long-term maintenance surface without a linked RFC.
> **Fix:** Link an RFC describing the CP indexer design before landing.

### 🔵 Advisory

**Import ordering** — `from vllm.distributed import get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size` is placed after local `vllm.models.*` imports in `indexer_aiter.py` instead of in sorted/isort order. Run `pre-commit` (yapf + ruff check/isort) to fix.

**Missing trailing newline** — `indexer_aiter_cp.py` ends without a trailing newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). Add one.

---

### Architecture Concerns

**`reuse-existing-internal-api-over-reimplementation`**
- `dist.all_reduce(..., op=MAX, group=get_tp_group().device_group)` reimplements a collective that `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` already provides. Use the canonical API.
- `select_aiter_cp_indexer_impl_cls` in `indexer_aiter_cp.py` duplicates the same env-var + TP>1 gating and log message already present in `select_aiter_indexer_impl_cls`. Remove the duplicate or consolidate to a single dispatch site.
- `score.fill_(float('-inf'))` after `self._new_score(...)` allocates two full score buffers every forward; consider pre-allocating in `__init__`.

**`gate-feature-on-upstream-kernel-readiness`**
Same as #57832: the MAX-allreduce-over-`-inf` pattern is a manual workaround for the absence of a CP-aware sparse-indexer primitive. The entire `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl` subclass and `select_aiter_cp_indexer_impl_cls` dispatcher exist only to host this workaround. Mark clearly as experimental and track the upstream CP primitive as a prerequisite.

**`minimal-fix-over-parallel-class-proliferation`**
The CP behavior is a single `forward()` branch (shard scoring + allreduce vs. full scoring). Consider folding it into the base `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterImpl.forward()` behind `if self.cp_enabled:` (set from the env var at `__init__`), eliminating the subclass and the extra dispatch branch.

**`drop-in-replacement-over-invasive-module-swap`**
The `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl.forward()` override relies on several base-class attributes (`_new_score`, `_table_rows`, `topk_indices_buffer`, `init_blocks`, `local_blocks`, etc.) that are not shown in the diff. Verify these are the actual base-class API names; otherwise the class-swap breaks at runtime.

**`deep-logic-bugs`**
- `indexer_aiter_cp.py:151` — In the prefill branch, `super().forward()` is called with `decode_page16_block_table=None` while `md.num_decodes` may be > 0. The base `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterImpl.forward()` still evaluates `md.num_decodes > 0` and may assert/deref `decode_page16_block_table`, causing a crash in mixed decode+prefill batches.
- `indexer_aiter_cp.py:126` — `shard_bt` compacts owned blocks into contiguous columns, so `pa_sparse_block_score_decode` writes `shard_score` at contiguous indices. But the scatter `score[..., owned_cols[:n_owned]] = shard_score[..., :n_owned]` assumes `shard_score`'s block axis is also contiguous. If the kernel uses global-indexed columns, the source slice is wrong. The comment and code make contradictory assumptions — verify the kernel's output layout.

---

+            get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size(),
+        )
+        return MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl
     return MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterImpl

@@ -0,0 +1,182 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MiniMax-M3 context-parallel AITER indexer for ROCm.
+
+Each TP rank scores its own round-robin shard of KV blocks via
+``minimax_m3_index_decode_score`` with a shard block table, scatters the
+results into a global-shape score tensor pre-filled with ``-inf``, and a MAX
+allreduce across the TP group fills the remaining positions. The complete score
+tensor is forwarded to ``pa_sparse_block_topk`` directly; the separate
+``pa_sparse_block_score_decode`` call is skipped.
+
+Enabled by ``VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1`` when the AITER indexer is
+selected (fp8 index cache, gfx950, TP>1).
+"""
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.distributed import get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_tp_group
+from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.indexer_aiter import (
+    MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterImpl,
+    select_aiter_indexer_impl_cls,
+)
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.common.indexer import MiniMaxM3IndexerMetadata
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl(MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterImpl):
+    """AITER indexer with context-parallel decode scoring for ROCm.
+
+    Decode: each rank scores its 1/world_size shard via the fp8 MFMA kernel,
+    scatters into a global score tensor, MAX allreduce reconstructs all
+    positions, ``pa_sparse_block_topk`` runs on the complete scores.
+
+    Prefill: unchanged, delegates to base AITER impl.
+    """
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        index_query: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        decode_page16_block_table: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        prefill_page16_block_table: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor | None, torch.Tensor | None]:
+        from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+
+        pa_sparse_block_score_decode = rocm_aiter_ops.pa_sparse_block_score_decode
+        pa_sparse_block_topk = rocm_aiter_ops.pa_sparse_block_topk
+
+        attn_metadata = get_forward_context().attn_metadata
+        if not isinstance(attn_metadata, dict):
+            return None, None
+
+        md = attn_metadata[self.index_cache.prefix]
+        assert isinstance(md, MiniMaxM3IndexerMetadata)
+        num_tokens = md.num_actual_tokens
+        nd = md.num_decode_tokens
+        iq = index_query[:num_tokens].view(
+            -1, self.num_index_heads, self.index_head_dim
+        )
+        kv = self.index_cache.kv_cache
+
+        buf = self.topk_indices_buffer
+        if buf is None:
+            buf = torch.empty(
+                (self.num_index_heads, num_tokens, self.topk_blocks),
+                dtype=torch.int32,
+                device=iq.device,
+            )
+
+        decode_topk: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        prefill_topk: torch.Tensor | None = None
+
+        if md.num_decodes > 0:
+            d = md.decode
+            assert d is not None
+            assert decode_page16_block_table is not None
+
+            world_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+            rank = get_tp_group().rank_in_group
+
+            max_blocks = d.block_table.shape[1]
+
+            # During cudagraph capture or when this rank owns no blocks
+            # (short sequences where rank >= max_blocks), fall through to
+            # the base AITER impl which handles these cases correctly.
+            if (torch.compiler.is_compiling()
+                    or max_blocks == 0
+                    or rank >= max_blocks):
+                return super().forward(
+                    index_query,
+                    decode_page16_block_table=decode_page16_block_table,
+                    prefill_page16_block_table=prefill_page16_block_table,
+                )
+
+            # Round-robin shard: rank r owns global blocks r, r+W, r+2W, ...
+            owned_cols = torch.arange(
+                rank, max_blocks, world_size,
+                dtype=d.block_table.dtype,
+                device=d.block_table.device,
+            )
+            shard_bt = d.block_table[:, owned_cols]
+
+            # Allocate global score tensor pre-filled with -inf.
+            score = self._new_score(nd, d.max_seq_len)
+            score.fill_(float("-inf"))
+
+            # Score owned blocks. shard_score uses d.max_seq_len so its
+            # block-axis width (score_block_width) matches the global score,
+            # making owned_cols column indices directly valid for both tensors.
+            shard_score = self._new_score(nd, d.max_seq_len)
+            pa_sparse_block_score_decode(
+                iq[:nd],
+                kv,
+                shard_score,
+                shard_bt,
+                d.seq_lens,
+                init_blocks=self.init_blocks,
+                local_blocks=self.local_blocks,
+                query_len=d.decode_query_len,
+                max_seq_len=d.max_seq_len,
+            )
+            # Scatter per-block scores into global tensor at owned column positions.
+            n_owned = min(len(owned_cols), shard_score.shape[-1])
+            score[..., owned_cols[:n_owned]] = shard_score[..., :n_owned]
+
+            # MAX allreduce reconstructs full global scores.
+            dist.all_reduce(
+                score,
+                op=dist.ReduceOp.MAX,
+                group=get_tp_group().device_group,
+            )
+
+            decode_topk = buf[:, :nd, :]
+            sparse_bt, sparse_ctx = self._table_rows(0, nd)
+            pa_sparse_block_topk(
+                score,
+                decode_topk,
+                decode_page16_block_table,
+                d.seq_lens,
+                sparse_bt,
+                sparse_ctx,
+                max_seq_len=d.max_seq_len,
+                block_size=self.block_size,
+                query_len=d.decode_query_len,
+                num_kv_heads=self.num_kv_heads,
+                pages_per_block=self.pages_per_block,
+            )
+
+        if md.num_prefills > 0:
+            _, prefill_topk = super().forward(
+                index_query,
+                decode_page16_block_table=None,
+                prefill_page16_block_table=prefill_page16_block_table,
+            )
+
+        return decode_topk, prefill_topk
+
+
+def select_aiter_cp_indexer_impl_cls(
+    **kwargs,
+) -> type[MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl] | None:
+    """Return the CP AITER impl if the env var and base AITER conditions hold."""
+    if not (
+        get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size() > 1
+        and envs.VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP
+    ):
+        return None
+    if select_aiter_indexer_impl_cls(**kwargs) is None:
+        return None
+    logger.info_once(
+        "MiniMax M3 indexer: selected AITER CP (context-parallel, ROCm) "
+        "[topk_blocks=%d, tp=%d]",
+        kwargs.get("topk_blocks", "?"),
+        get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size(),
+    )
+    return MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl
\ No newline at end of file

## PR Pundit Review — [#57840](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57840)

**5 rule violations · 5 architecture concerns · 2 files reviewed**
Rules checked: 32 (27 passed, 5 failed)

---

### 🔴 Blockers

**`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter_cp.py:1-12` — Missing benchmark / description**
This performance-affecting change (new context-parallel AITER indexer for ROCm) provides no reproducible benchmark steps or before/after metrics. Reviewers have consistently blocked such PRs.
> **Fix:** Add before/after latency and `gsm8k` accuracy numbers for the CP AITER indexer path, and reproduce the benchmark command in the PR description.

**`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter.py:601-614` — `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP` not registered in `vllm/envs.py`**
`envs.VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP` is accessed but not declared as a canonical `VLLM_`-prefixed attribute.
> **Fix:** Add `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP: bool = False` to `vllm/envs.py`.

**`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter_cp.py:1-30` — New cross-cutting parallelism mechanism without RFC**
Introduces a new CP indexer dispatch abstraction (`select_aiter_cp_indexer_impl_cls`) as a long-term maintenance surface without a linked RFC.
> **Fix:** Link an RFC describing the CP indexer design before landing.

### 🔵 Advisory

**Import ordering** — `from vllm.distributed import get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size` is placed after local `vllm.models.*` imports in `indexer_aiter.py` instead of in sorted/isort order. Run `pre-commit` (yapf + ruff check/isort) to fix.

**Missing trailing newline** — `indexer_aiter_cp.py` ends without a trailing newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). Add one.

---

### Architecture Concerns

**`reuse-existing-internal-api-over-reimplementation`**
- `dist.all_reduce(..., op=MAX, group=get_tp_group().device_group)` reimplements a collective that `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` already provides. Use the canonical API.
- `select_aiter_cp_indexer_impl_cls` in `indexer_aiter_cp.py` duplicates the same env-var + TP>1 gating and log message already present in `select_aiter_indexer_impl_cls`. Remove the duplicate or consolidate to a single dispatch site.
- `score.fill_(float('-inf'))` after `self._new_score(...)` allocates two full score buffers every forward; consider pre-allocating in `__init__`.

**`gate-feature-on-upstream-kernel-readiness`**
Same as #57832: the MAX-allreduce-over-`-inf` pattern is a manual workaround for the absence of a CP-aware sparse-indexer primitive. The entire `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl` subclass and `select_aiter_cp_indexer_impl_cls` dispatcher exist only to host this workaround. Mark clearly as experimental and track the upstream CP primitive as a prerequisite.

**`minimal-fix-over-parallel-class-proliferation`**
The CP behavior is a single `forward()` branch (shard scoring + allreduce vs. full scoring). Consider folding it into the base `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterImpl.forward()` behind `if self.cp_enabled:` (set from the env var at `__init__`), eliminating the subclass and the extra dispatch branch.

**`drop-in-replacement-over-invasive-module-swap`**
The `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl.forward()` override relies on several base-class attributes (`_new_score`, `_table_rows`, `topk_indices_buffer`, `init_blocks`, `local_blocks`, etc.) that are not shown in the diff. Verify these are the actual base-class API names; otherwise the class-swap breaks at runtime.

**`deep-logic-bugs`**
- `indexer_aiter_cp.py:151` — In the prefill branch, `super().forward()` is called with `decode_page16_block_table=None` while `md.num_decodes` may be > 0. The base `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterImpl.forward()` still evaluates `md.num_decodes > 0` and may assert/deref `decode_page16_block_table`, causing a crash in mixed decode+prefill batches.
- `indexer_aiter_cp.py:126` — `shard_bt` compacts owned blocks into contiguous columns, so `pa_sparse_block_score_decode` writes `shard_score` at contiguous indices. But the scatter `score[..., owned_cols[:n_owned]] = shard_score[..., :n_owned]` assumes `shard_score`'s block axis is also contiguous. If the kernel uses global-indexed columns, the source slice is wrong. The comment and code make contradictory assumptions — verify the kernel's output layout.
